quotes.text: When a capability becomes expected, it stops being strategic and that transition is now complete. The market no longer values technical implementation. It values economic stewardship.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's core thesis about where partner value has moved.

quotes.text: If you deploy co-pilot into a company that hasn't redesigned its workflows, adoption will stay low and no value will be created.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Separates feature activation from real business transformation.

quotes.text: Identity is the control plane of the modern enterprise. If you do not control the identity, you do not control the access and you certainly cannot govern the system.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why identity lifecycle management is the base of tenant stewardship.

quotes.text: Governance is not overhead. It is risk reduction and cost prevention. Once a customer understands that, they will fund it. The cost of not governing is invisible until it turns into a crisis.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives partners a clear argument for selling governance as a funded service.

quotes.text: The future ISP is not a technical implementer. You do not implement Microsoft 365, you operate it. You do not deploy co-pilot, you govern it. You do not manage licenses, you optimize them.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up the shift from implementation to economic stewardship in three contrasts.

takeaways: CSP margin compression, the direct EA transition and automation such as Autopilot, Lighthouse and embedded Copilot are commoditizing Microsoft implementation work.
License resellers, migration factories and feature-driven MSPs are losing ground because they sell capabilities customers now assume or can buy anywhere.
Partners who build economic telemetry, architectural stewardship and AI value governance move from episodic projects to retainers and own the customer's cost-to-value relationship.
hook: Microsoft partners still competing on certifications and deployment skills are watching margins shrink as CSP changes, automation and Copilot commoditize implementation. This episode helps consultants, MSPs and ISP leaders understand why technical excellence is now table stakes and how a tenant stewardship model built on economic outcomes creates defensible, recurring revenue.
